ambiguities.description: The phrase 'against gross' is ambiguous: it could mean the $900 is deducted from gross before the 80% net percentage is calculated, or it could mean the $900 counts inside the $2,500 expense cap. The deal note confirms this was actually disputed by WME and resolved with a $720 concession — consistent with the venue having applied reading (p1) and splitting the difference.

plausibleReadings.summary: Recoup is deducted from gross as a separate line item before the 80% percentage is applied, independent of the expense cap.
plausibleReadings.impact: Venue-favorable. Reduces the net base on which 80% is calculated, costing artist roughly $720 on a typical gross — exactly matching the documented concession amount.

plausibleReadings.summary: Recoup counts inside the $2,500 expense cap, not as an additional deduction from gross.
plausibleReadings.impact: Artist-favorable. Cap acts as a ceiling on all venue charges including marketing; artist is made whole by ~$720 relative to reading p1.

ambiguities.suggestedClarification: Is the $900 marketing recoup deducted from gross as a standalone line before 80% is applied, or does it count inside the $2,500 expense cap? Please confirm in writing before advancing the next show to avoid a repeat of the 3/19/25 dispute.

sourceText: $5,000 vs 80% of net after expenses, whichever greater. Expenses capped $2,500. Hospitality cap $500. +$1,000 bonus over $25k gross. Marketing recoup of $900 against gross. (Note added 3/19/25: this deal email was ambiguous — recoup interpretation disputed by WME, resolved with $720 concession.)
